newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia lending rate raised to 9.6 pct vs 7.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatia lending rate raised to 9.6 pct vs 7.8 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate rebounded to 9.6 percent from 7.8 percent in Wednesday's slow trade, lifted by a larger share of term loans.
Daily transactions totalled 9.7 million kuna, leaving an extra 70 million on offer. Half of the trade was call money granted at 7.0 percent.
Creditors granted one-month loans at 13.5 percent and monthly funds at 18 percent.
Previous two-week funds were rolled over at a 9.0 percent rate.

The central bank calculated kuna mid-rates for Thursday weaker at 6.5598 against the dollar and firmer at 3.5657 against the German mark after purchasing a large amount of marks and some dollars from the banking sector.
